extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or graduate students in mathematical logic / computability theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and standard constructions for primitive/partial/general recursive functions, enumeration of computable functions, Kleene normal form, the halting problem, and computably enumerable sets. A textbook-level treatment aimed at teaching how to define, encode, and reason about computable and partially computable functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous recursion
rubrics_metrics.description: Define multiple functions together via mutual recurrence, e.g. h0(x,0)=f0(x), h1(x,0)=f1(x), and h0(x,y+1)=g0(x,y,h0(x,y),h1(x,y)), h1(x,y+1)=g1(x,y,h0(x,y),h1(x,y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an instance of simultaneous recursion; multiple functions' successor steps can depend on the current values of all the functions being defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course-of-values recursion
rubrics_metrics.description: Define h(x,0)=f(x) and h(x,y+1)=g(x,y,〈h(x,0),...,h(x,y)〉), or succinctly h(x,y)=g(x,y,〈h(x,0),...,h(x,y−1)〉).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In computing the successor step, h may use the entire sequence of previously computed values. Example: allow h(x,y) to reference h(x,k(x,y)) for some k that may be < y. Think about simulating these using ordinary primitive recursion (possible but tricky).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive recursion with changing parameters (side values)
rubrics_metrics.description: A more flexible primitive recursion allowing parameter changes: h(x,0)=f(x) and h(x,y+1)=g(x,y,h(k(x),y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This variant can be simulated with ordinary primitive recursion; simulation is tricky and may require 'unwinding' the computation manually for a construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumeration of primitive recursive functions (coding of notations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign symbolic notations to primitive recursive functions and code notations as natural numbers via a coding scheme (e.g., #(0)=⟨0⟩, #(S)=⟨1⟩, #(...composition...) = ⟨3,k,l,#(H),#(G0),...⟩, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every code is assigned a natural number; some numbers do not correspond to notations. Use the codes to enumerate unary primitive recursive functions fi by taking the function with notation coded as i when valid, otherwise the constant 0. Note that repetitions occur (same function may have multiple notations) and there is no computable way to avoid these repetitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagonalization to produce non-primitive recursive computable functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an effective enumeration of unary primitive recursive functions f0,f1,... with computable evaluation g(x,y)=fx(y), define h(x)=g(x,x)+1 to obtain a computable function h that differs from every fi at i, hence computable but not primitive recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an effective Cantor diagonalization argument showing primitive recursive functions do not exhaust computable functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial recursive functions — treatment of partiality (notations ↓, ↑, ≃)
rubrics_metrics.description: When allowing partial functions, denote definedness by f(x) ↓ and undefinedness by f(x) ↑; use f(x) ≃ g(x) to mean both undefined or both defined and equal. Composition/recursion definitions require replacing '=' by '≃' to account for undefinedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the convention that h(g0(x),...,gk(x)) is defined iff each gi is defined at x and h is defined at those gi outputs. This modification allows the primitive recursion and composition clauses to be applied in the partial setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbounded search (µ operator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a (possibly partial) function f(x,z), µx f(x,z) is the least x such that f(0,z),...,f(x,z) are all defined and f(x,z)=0; undefined if no such x exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational intuition: compute f(0,z),f(1,z),... until a 0 is returned. If any intermediate computation never halts, the µ-computation also does not halt. For relations R, µx R(x,z)=µx(1−χR(x,z)) returns the least x with R(x,z) true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of partial recursive functions (closure properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of partial recursive functions is the smallest set of partial functions N^k→N containing 0, successor, projections, and closed under composition, primitive recursion, and unbounded search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some partial recursive functions happen to be total; those total ones are called recursive (or total recursive) functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General recursive functions (regular functions and restricted search)
rubrics_metrics.description: A total function f(x,z) is regular if for every z there is an x with f(x,z)=0. The general recursive functions are the smallest set containing 0,S,projections and closed under composition, primitive recursion, and unbounded search applied only to regular functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every general recursive function is total. Though definitions differ from the set of (total) recursive functions, both sets coincide (the difference is illusory historically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleene's Normal Form Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist a primitive recursive relation T(e,x,s) and a primitive recursive function U(s) such that for every partial recursive function f, for some e: f(x) ≃ U(µs T(e,x,s)) for every x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuition: T(e,x,s) checks that s codes a computation of the program e on input x; U(s) extracts the output from the coded computation. The theorem shows only a single unbounded search is needed to define any partial recursive function, and motivates the notation φe(x) ≃ U(µs T(e,x,s)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Halting function and undecidability of the halting problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Define h(e,x)=1 if computation e halts on input x, and 0 otherwise. Theorem: h is not computable (not partial recursive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs via diagonalization: (1) assume h computable to build a total universal function Un' leading to contradiction with no total universal function; (2) construct a partial function g(x) that uses h(x,x) to derive contradiction about whether g(e) is defined. Turing-machine style proof: build G that runs a hypothetical halting decider H and does the opposite behavior, leading to contradiction when run on its own code.

rubrics_metrics.name: s-m-n theorem (parameterization / program specialization)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each n,m there is a primitive recursive function smn such that for every e and a0,...,am−1: φ_{smn(e,a0,...,am−1)}(y0,...,yn−1) ≃ φ_{e}(a0,...,am−1,y0,...,yn−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: smn acts on program codes; given a program for an (m+n)-ary function and fixed first m inputs, it returns a program for the remaining n-ary function. smn is primitive recursive and effectively finds the code of the specialized program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal partial computable function (enumeration of partial computable functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a partial computable function Un(e,x) that is universal: every partial computable f(x) satisfies f(x) ≃ Un(e,x) for some e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take Un(e,x) ≃ U(µs T(e,x,s)) from Kleene normal form. This gives an effective enumeration (φ0,φ1,...) of partial computable functions. Note: Un is partial (not total).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonexistence of a universal total computable function
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no total (everywhere-defined) computable function Un'(k,x) that enumerates all total computable functions (i.e., for each total computable f there would be k with f(x)=Un'(k,x) for all x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by diagonalization: define d(x)=Un'(x,x)+1 which would be total computable and differ from every Un'(k,·) at x=k, contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical ways to show a function is computable
rubrics_metrics.description: Two acceptable approaches: (1) rigorously describe a Turing machine or partial recursive function that computes it, or (2) informally describe an algorithm and appeal to the Church–Turing thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a balance: provide intuitive yet rigorous proofs that specify enough detail so a Turing machine or recursive construction could be obtained in principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding computations (encoding descriptions and computation records)
rubrics_metrics.description: In every model of computation one can (1) describe definitions of computable functions systematically, (2) describe complete records of computations, (3) test whether a putative record matches a computation, and (4) extract the output from such a record. These descriptions and records can be coded as natural numbers; the relation 's codes the record of computation of program e on input x' and the function mapping a record code to its output are computable (indeed primitive recursive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This coding underlies Kleene's normal form theorem and the construction of universal functions and enumerations of computable functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computable sets (decidable sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set S of natural numbers is computable iff its characteristic function χ_S is computable (χ_S(x)=1 if x∈S, 0 otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, these sets are called decidable. Distinguish between Turing machines computing partial functions (may not halt) and machines deciding sets (must always halt with 0/1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computably enumerable (c.e./r.e.) sets — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A set is computably enumerable if it is empty or the range of a computable function (equivalently, the range of a partial computable function or a primitive recursive function).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of a computable f enumerating S as S={f(0),f(1),...}; enumerations may repeat and need not be in increasing order. If S is computable then it is c.e. (construct an enumerator), and c.e. sets are sometimes called semi-decidable: membership yields eventually a 'yes', non-membership yields no 'no'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of computably enumerable sets
rubrics_metrics.description: For a set S of naturals, the following are equivalent: (1) S is computably enumerable; (2) S is the range of a partial computable function; (3) S is empty or the range of a primitive recursive function; (4) S is the domain of a partial computable function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Kleene normal form: express an enumerating partial computable function φ_e as U(µs T(e,x,s)) and build primitive recursive enumerators or show S equals the domain of some φ_e. For (1)⇔(4) construct g(y)=µx(f(x)=y) to convert an enumerator into a semi-decision procedure; for (4)⇒(1) take S as domain {x:φ_e(x)↓} and show it's the range of a computable enumerator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of normal form (T and U) to convert between enumerators and domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Given φ_e(x)=U(µs T(e,x,s)), express the range or domain of φ_e in primitive recursive terms by combining T and U to build primitive recursive functions whose range equals S, or to derive semi-decision procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete constructions: define f(z) to return U((z)_1) if T(e,(z)_0,(z)_1) holds, else a fixed a; this yields a primitive recursive enumerator for the range of φ_e.
